Today, we have a fantastic cultural scene that is only lacking in access; Seniors and differently abled people do not have the type of access that we should strive for. Beyond this, affordability and safety are areas that need more support.
explanations.av_conditions: Like with bike lanes, companies operating abroad, not paying a shred of taxes here have monopolised transportation such that the city has lost revenue from taxi licenses and the consumer is experiencing the enshitification of provided services. If autonomous taxis operate here where are the profits?
explanations.budget_gap_first: not spend a billion dollars on FIFA, for example
explanations.business_attraction: Unfortunately the choices here pigeon hole the answer. The CITY should focus on sector strategy and use citywide fundamentals as that reinforces the social-business relationship. However the tax code at provincial and federal levels will outweigh the level of attraction major employers see from City
explanations.business_climate: Toronto is the business capital, yet Canada is experiencing a brain drain. We need to retain those tempted to leave, and keep the arrivals here and happy. The best way to reinforce the business climate is to make the city more liveable, inviting workers, reinforcing business and social relationships
explanations.capital_project_delays: How many of the "capital projects" in question are directly due to developers not covering the increased associated expenses of their projects. Politicians approving projects in this city have not done their due diligence in ensuring that development doesn't come with generational debt.
explanations.capital_transparency: We are long overdue for absolute transparency about operation and financial updates. We have the technology to efficiently disseminate relevant information about how and where our tax dollars are building the city projects we need.
explanations.construction_capacity: If we want to keep building the way we have we need infrastructure, but we can't reasonably pay for all of these public projects at the rate the development goes. Maintenance and retirement budgets need to be prioritised over the urgency for another immediate build. We end up paying more long term
explanations.cycling_network: We need to examine the relationship between the costs of bike lanes and the use of them by delivery companies. Commuters and delivery workers do not share the same use of the roadway. The direction the city's designs in should not benefit a handful of companies at the taxpayer's expense
explanations.encampment_removal: We are not going to have encampments near schools or parks. After a certain point on the streets the hardships are such that many of the people in question lack the mental acuity to understand their situation as dire enough to ask for, or accept, the help they need.
explanations.housing_as_of_right: Communities should be given agency in determining what their neighbourhoods look like. This means increasing consultation and outreach such that we are confident that we are building to the desire and to the benefit of people who are already living there, and not building to meet a statistic number
explanations.housing_city_role: There's a very serious need to reestablish the dwindling middle class in Canada, this starts at home in Toronto by empowering residents to move away from long term rental and into home ownership.
explanations.housing_cost_reduction: Homeowners(not faceless landlords) living their residences renting out fewer than 3 total units will be exempt from paying tax on rent. This keeps the cost of rent down, as well as strengthening the individual homeowner such that they can increase the housing supply.
explanations.housing_density_location: The city is at a mass now where planning is crucial, we don't have the infrastructure to further densify without the cost to the taxpayer snowballing. We have provided the transit to remote areas, now developers can foot the infrastructure bill for the densification of those areas.
explanations.housing_intervention: We can't allow indiscriminate building because there is a housing problem. Empowering homeowners to expand and build new units will create the type of communities that will provide long term solutions, while empowering corporate development will create and austere and dependent communities.
explanations.infrastructure_backlog: Charge the developers for the increased strain they've put on our systems. Sewers, bridges, transformers etc are their costs if they bring such a magnitude of change to the projected maintenance and retirement budgets of public infrastructure.
explanations.infrastructure_revenue: Almost 40% of the population of the province lives in the Toronto area. We will not beg the province to get our own money back; especially when the province has clear interests in undermining the city's agency in directing the uses of our public spaces.
explanations.performance_metric: Voters should assess performance of their politicians by looking at the changes in the quality of their communities, neighbourhood and daily lives over a term. Do you as a voter feel considered?
explanations.police_budget: We need to reassess how the money is being spent. We need police officers that belong to the community, who live here and have a stake in their own city.
explanations.property_tax_growth: Our most recent property tax hike was such that we need a cool down over the next council term.
explanations.protest_access: The City of Toronto & the TPS must respect our right to peaceful assembly and protect it without compromising the safety of the city and its residents and visitors. The city thereby also has the responsibility to acknowledge and promptly address the concerns brought forth in said protests.
explanations.provincial_approach: Years ago the provincial government amalgamated the city reducing our agency and access to our politicians. Today the provincial government makes it clear that it will operate as it sees fit within the city; in direct opposition of local sentiment. The provincial government should fear secession.
explanations.public_realm_priority: International visitors are frequently appalled at the level of filth and disrepair visible in our city. Toronto quickly became a world class city, unfortunately we do not emulate that in our aesthetic and it is noticed by visitors. If we want to attract business then we should clean up, and shovel.
explanations.revenue_source: Road tolls for non residents. Uber and other tech companies operating should be taxed accordingly to their road use.
explanations.road_pricing: Homeowners and residential occupants with vehicles registered to their adresses within the core should be exempt from congestion charges.
explanations.safety_investment: Despite the hyper focus on the drug addicted-homeless stereotype of street safety, we forget that they do not account for the majority of the crime. Rehab and intervention is required, but foremost; we need to the police to rid the streets of the dealers, actually respond to calls, and enforce law.
explanations.service_delivery_model: If we do not have direct delivery of services then we will lose the ability to hold accountable those providing the services.
explanations.street_space_priority: Considerations for the elderly and the disabled are first concern.
explanations.strong_mayor_powers: As it related to the previous question, this is a controversial political tool that can be easily abused, however it would seem the need for it is dependent on how other levels of government are interacting with the city at that time.
explanations.surveillance_tech: parking enforcement should be on foot; this one is personal; they don't even check the windshield for the tag half the time, im tired of the TPS parking ticket petition form that comes back as "penalty cancelled" every time the automated-reader missed the permit clearly displayed in my windshield.
explanations.technology_investment: Thinking about the differently-abled, the elderly, and generally those who lose their minds with online forms; The city MUST offer accessible and convenient services without the concerns of technological investment and digitisation risking that convenient access.
explanations.transit_funding_priority: The vitrolite colour tiles and the retro mid century look that define so many of our stations, and the brutalist concrete shapes of the arcades falling to the platforms deserve restoration. explanations.ward_commitment_target: We have fewer homeless individuals than we do Airbnb units, this is fundamentally wrong. With her distinctive pink hair and unwavering commitment to equity, she has become a recognizable voice for progressive change in Toronto's diverse communities.
answers.ward_commitment_target: Implement two fully funded community-led development projects including public-realm improvements on municipal land by December 2029

explanations.arts_culture_support: The best tools for supporting arts and culture is affordable housing, affordable and efficient public transit, and the preservation of existing venues and workspaces from demolition or displacement.
explanations.av_conditions: Autonomous taxi services should simply not operate in Toronto, or anywhere else.
explanations.budget_gap_first: Successive reviews have found that Toronto's budget challenges are overall the result of constrained revenue, rather than excessive spending. While there are specific budget areas that we can de-prioritize, overall, the City needs access to a greater variety of progressive revenue tools.
explanations.capital_project_delays: Toronto cannot afford to defer needed capital projects. Nor can we squander public money and trust delivering these projects badly and slowly. The City needs stronger project management and procurement, more rigorous oversight of contracts, and transparent reporting when schedules change.
explanations.capital_transparency: If we are spending public money on public projects, then the public has a right to know where that money is going, and if projects are on time and on budget. However, this reporting must be a tool for stronger long-term financial and project management, not just numbers after the fact.
explanations.cycling_network: The solution to Toronto's traffic woes is to increase the number of different ways people can move around efficiently and safely. This means thoughtful expansion of our protected cycling network, in addition to significant investment in public transit.
explanations.encampment_removal: Not automatically. If the person voluntarily accepts a truly suitable indoor space, then we should help them move. If they don't, the City should not immediately move to eviction, but should instead work to understand why the person is refusing and work to remove the barrier.
explanations.housing_as_of_right: Yes, but not the same density across the city. Permitting should accommodate gentle density in neighbourhoods, with and greater density along transit corridors, while preserving tress and public space in all areas.
explanations.housing_city_role: Toronto must use as many of its resources as possible to create and preserve permanently affordable housing. This means both expanding its role as a direct provider and partnering with community-based non-profit partners to meet specific community needs.
explanations.housing_density_location: Toronto has a lot of space, but very little of it is downtown. Detatched-house neighbourhoods cannot exist as museum pieces while we stack human beings in boxes in designated growth centres. Our most vibrant neighbourhoods and streets feature a mix of housing types and heights.
explanations.housing_intervention: Housing is a human right. Leaving housing affordability up to private interests has not served Toronto very well over the past many years. Non-market, public models including co-op housing, supportive housing, and community housing are essential to addressing our housing crisis.
explanations.infrastructure_backlog: Toronto's infrastructure deficit is the result of refusing to provide the city with the revenue it needs to maintain our assets. Letting infrastructure continue to deteriorate is not the answer, nor is selling these assets. We need to raise the revenue necessary for maintenance and invest in growth.
explanations.infrastructure_revenue: Toronto cannot afford to defer maintenance while we wait for other levels of government to come to our rescue. We must both use the revenue tools we have and fight for more tools to keep our roads, transit, libraries, community centres, parks and housing in a state of good repair.
explanations.performance_metric: We have thousands of homes being built in Ward 19. What we lack are the public-realm improvements to support our burgeoning population. This means preserving, cleaning, and maintaining our existing public spaces and investing in the infrastructure and public amenities to support our population.
explanations.police_budget: Toronto cannot keep adding money to the police budget without interrogating what we are asking police to do and whether the police service is the best service provider for these tasks. In the case of activity related to mental health crises, homelessness, and addiction, it is not.
explanations.property_tax_growth: Toronto needs predictable revenue growth to maintain services and address our infrastructure backlog. Property taxes should generally keep pace with inflation or grow slightly faster while the City pursues more progressive revenue sources. Ultimately, we need better revenue sources.
explanations.protest_access: I am in favour of fundamental rights to freedom of expression and freedom of association.
explanations.public_realm_priority: I reject the proposition that we cannot have all of these investments, starting with the basics.
explanations.revenue_source: Few people like paying taxes. But Toronto needs access to stable revenue sources that grow with the economy. Property taxes -- with adequate relief for seniors -- should remain a key part of our financial ecosystem, but Toronto should seek authority for broader progressive municipal revenue tools.
explanations.road_pricing: Road pricing (tolls or congestion charging), works best to reduce traffic and raise revenue when it forms part of an overall transportation strategy, rather than as a simple user-fee or tax. So in addition to devoting revenue from road-pricing to transportation, we must invest in transit.
explanations.safety_investment: The intervention that will most improve public safety is housing. Following that, the wrap-around services that support people living in crisis AND public-space management.
explanations.service_delivery_model: Toronto should deliver core public services directly whenever we can do so efficiently. Using City staff, equipment, and expertise allows us to retain institutional knowledge and maintain quality and accountability.
explanations.street_space_priority: When street space is limited, we should prioritize the ways of moving that allow the largest number of people to move, while also protecting essential access, such as emergency vehicles, deliveries, accessibility and trade.
explanations.technology_investment: I am not in favour of replacing front-line staff with AI tools that lack the nuance, knowledge, and empathy to handle a complex city like Toronto. Systems do not hold departments accountable -- they allow leadership to hold departments accountable. I think that is an important distinction.
explanations.transit_funding_priority: In a world where we had just one pot of transit-funding money, I'd prioritize service, with state-of-good-repair protected as an essential investment and other levels of government funding their share of rapid-transit expansion.
explanations.ward_commitment_target: You can see my ten specific, time-bound priorities on my website: jennieworden.ca.
